honors.title: Outstanding Academic Achievement in Computer Science
Distill Your Idea Hackathon -  Team Lead and Developer - Winning Group
honors.description:
Distill Your Idea was Bakersfield's first Hackathon open to the public. The event consisted of a weekend of technological innovation and creation of an idea related to alcohol, breweries, or alcohol safety.

Out team built a prototype and developed a business plan for a mobile first web application designed to solve the problem of finding an event to attend at a local bar or brewery, and local businesses to gather feedback from users about types events they would be interested in attending. Currently, there is no easy technological solution to the problem of finding local nightlife events that favor those 21 and older. Our app, "What's Happening?", changes that by taking advantage of Facebook's Graph API. 

The app used Facebook for authentication, page information and event information. After manually collecting a single Facebook Page ID, the app can then have access to the Page's events listed on Facebook and then is no more manual collection needed. Our Group then put together a list of page IDs of local bars and breweries to pull data from. The app also featured a form to give feedback about a type of event users would like to see at a specific place from the ones collected. The app could then potentially post the suggested event type and location to Facebook, and count 'likes' on the post, therefore expanding the audience from app users to friends of app users or whoever has access to view the post. Our team also developed a business plan to potentially offer paid plans for businesses with Facebook pages listed in the app to gather data on user feedback, promote their events listed, or push their own questions about what types of events users would like to see at their business. The app would be free for users. Our team executed market research to validate the business plan.
honors.issuer: Issued by Kern Innovation and Technology · Apr 2016
